title: Data Preprocessing & Feature Engineering
description: Master data preparation: handling missing values, standard vs min-max scaling, categorical encoding, and preventing data leakage.

slides.title: Garbage In, Garbage Out 🧹
slides.content:
# Data Preprocessing & Cleaning

Real-world data is messy, incomplete, and noisy. Algorithms cannot interpret raw text strings or NaN values directly.

### The Core Cleaning Steps:
* **Handling Missing Data:** Deletion (dropping rows/columns) or Imputation (filling missing values with mean, median, or KNN estimates).
* **Categorical Encoding:** Converting discrete text labels into numerical vectors via One-Hot Encoding (for nominal classes) or Ordinal Encoding (for ranked classes).
* **Outlier Mitigation:** Clipping extreme values using interquartile ranges (IQR) or z-score thresholds.

slides.title: Feature Scaling Techniques ⚖️
slides.content:
# Comparing Feature Scaling Methods

When features have drastically different scales (e.g. Age: $18-80$ vs Salary: $\$20,000-\$500,000$), gradient descent will oscillate erratically. Scaling resolves this:

| Technique | Formula | Output Range | Outlier Sensitivity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Min-Max Normalization** | $x' = \frac{x - x_{\min}}{x_{\max} - x_{\min}}$ | $[0, 1]$ | High (outliers squeeze valid data into narrow sub-range) |
| **Standardization (Z-Score)**| $z = \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$ | Mean $\mu=0$, Variance $\sigma^2=1$ | Robust (preserves relative variance without bounded ceiling) |
| **Robust Scaling** | $x' = \frac{x - Q_2}{Q_3 - Q_1}$ | Centered at median | Highly robust (uses interquartile range resistant to extreme outliers) |

Standardization is preferred for neural networks and algorithms assuming Gaussian feature distributions.

quizData.question: Why is Standardization (Z-score scaling) often preferred over Min-Max scaling on datasets with extreme outliers?

options.text: It guarantees all feature values are strictly positive integers
It does not compress the inlier values into an imperceptibly tiny range due to extreme maximums
It automatically imputes all missing NaN values
It eliminates the need for gradient descent updates

quizData.explanation: Min-Max scaling uses min and max values directly; an extreme outlier will crush 99% of normal data into a narrow band between 0.0 and 0.05. Standardization avoids this bounding distortion.

slides.title: Feature Scaling with scikit-learn 🐍
slides.content: Here is how to properly scale features and encode categorical columns in Python:
slides.codeSnippet:
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder
import numpy as np

# Sample feature matrix: [Age, Income]
X = np.array([[25, 45000], [50, 120000], [35, 75000]])

scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)

print('Scaled features (mean=0, std=1):\n', X_scaled.round(2))

slides.title: Preventing Data Leakage ⚠️
slides.content:
## The Golden Rule of Preprocessing
**NEVER fit scalers or imputers on the entire dataset before splitting!**

If you call `scaler.fit(X_all)`, you leak information from the test set (mean, variance) into your training phase, leading to overly optimistic test metrics that crater in production.

*Always execute:* `X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)` and `X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)`.
